text:
alex: Quick follow-up to the gatekeeper RFC — thinking we should centralize version/compat checks in a lightweight gateway before routing to runtime. Keeps shims out of model infra and makes rollout easier.

matt: +1. Curious how much logic lives there vs feature flags. we don't want it to become another monolith.

sophia: Agree. Proposal: 1) header-based detection, 2) small transform hooks (JS/wasm), 3) metrics emitted for drop-in compatibility. :thumbsup:

alex: Sketch of rule:
```
if request.headers['X-Client-Version'] < '3.0.0':
  route = 'legacy-compat'
  apply_transform('envelope-unwrap')
else:
  route = 'native'
```

maria: Two operational notes: ensure trace propagation, and add a soft-fail mode that lets us monitor without routing yet. We should also rate-limit legacy paths to limit cost.

matt: Soft-fail mode sounds critical. Also add a tenant opt-in flag — some customers may want extended compat for longer.

sophia: For transforms, can we reuse existing sidecar code? keep runtime footprint small.

alex: Yes reusing sidecar code is ideal. Plan: prototype as small proxy service owned by eng-platform, deploy behind feature flag, run canary, then flip per-tenant. Runbook needed for rollback.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: gatekeeper-proxy v0.1 -> canary on staging

maria: I'll draft runbook + telemetry events (compat.path, compat.switch, compat.fail). putting first draft in RFC thread.

alex: perfect. assigning follow-ups: @maria runbook, @sophia transform interface, @matt telemetry hooks. schedule 30m sync tomorrow? :clock1:

matt: works for me.

sophia: yep.

maria: done, added calendar invite.
